title: Australian soccer league introduces penalty shootout bonus points for drawn games
content:
The Australian Championship, the second tier of the nation’s soccer league system, has introduced a ‘penalty shootout bonus point model’ with regular time draws going directly to spot kicks.

The new mechanism will mean that a ‘bonus point’ is on offer for the team which wins the penalty shootout, who will collect two points from the fixture, while the losing spot-kick side will collect just one point.

The league have said it is designed to create “genuine excitement, keeping supporters engaged to the final kick, and giving players rare high-pressure match experience”.

The matches will still be recorded as draws and there will be no extra-time played at the end of 90 minutes, but drawn matches will proceed straight to penalties to determine the extra point allocation.

The league differs from many traditional football divisions as it is held annually at the end of the third-tier National Premier Leagues (NPL) season, pitting the competition’s eight permanent members against the eight NPL premiers in a tournament consisting of a sixteen-team group stage and then an eight-team knockout stage.

In the group stage, teams are divided into four groups of four, with each team playing six games and the top two sides in each group advancing. In total, the Championship is played over two months at the end of the calendar year season.

The bonus-point format will only apply to the first phase of the competition before traditional knockout games are held.

Football Australia, the governing body for the nation’s sport, consulted the decision with its clubs and the Japanese Football Association (JFA) for its J1 100 Year Vision League (a shortened league tournament in the interim as the J1 League transitioned to an August-May format from its previous February-December editions) earlier this year.

Australia’s former top-level National Soccer League also used the penalty bonus-point format in the 1994-95 edition, and it has also been used in the Leagues Cup — annually held between clubs from the U.S.’s Major League Soccer (MLS) and Mexico’s Liga MX.
